Mariah Carey and Nick Cannon ’s 15-year-old twins, Moroccan and Monroe, threw a bit of shade at their 10 siblings in the trailer for Netflix’s upcoming reality show Raising the Cannons .

“Maybe if you didn’t have all these kids, you would have been back together,” Monroe told her dad while in a car together in one scene in the trailer, which was released on Tuesday, November 17.

Later, Moroccan added, “This lifestyle, I don’t think it’s sustainable in any way.”

Cannon, 46, and Carey, 57, met at the Teen Choice Awards in 2005 and later reconnected in 2008 on the set of Carey’s music video for “Bye Bye.” The pair tied the knot that April after just six weeks of dating and welcomed their twins in April 2011.

Cannon and Carey confirmed their separation in 2014.

“There is trouble in paradise. We have been living in separate houses for a few months,” the Wild n’ Out host said at the time.

Mariah Carey Shares Rare Insight Into Coparenting Twins With Nick Cannon

items.summary:
Ruby Franke ’s first parole hearing is around the corner—and her eldest daughter, Shari Franke , is already making her position clear to the parole board.

The former family blogger and her former business partner, Jodi Hildebrandt , are each scheduled to appear before the Utah Board of Pardons and Parole on December 7, 2026, three years after they were arrested on child abuse charges that shocked their online following. While the women were convicted on related charges, their cases will be reviewed separately.

Ahead of the hearings, Shari submitted a lengthy email to the board opposing parole for both her mother and Hildebrandt. She wrote that “three years cannot fix a lifetime of hurt.”

Here’s what to know about the parole hearings, Shari’s statement and where Ruby and Hildebrandt stand today.

Shari Franke Urges Parole Board to Deny Ruby Franke’s Release 
 In the email, Shari wrote that she last spoke with her mother face-to-face four years ago.

Ruby Franke, Jodi Hildebrandt's Friendship Timeline Amid Child Abuse Arrest 

“It’s been 4 years since I last talked face to face with Ruby. It was the most stressful experience of my life. She told me that through my speaking out against her publicly, I didn’t want to be part of the family,” she wrote.

Shari said she was “cut off from all my siblings” after going public with concerns about her mother and that she sensed “something terrible was happening” inside the home. items.summary:
Prosecutors in KJ Biermann ‘s sexual battery case have filed a motion opposing the transfer of his case to juvenile court, Us confirmed.

In court documents obtained by Us , the State of Georgia called 15-year-old Biermann’s alleged offenses “incredibly serious” and claimed that the teen exhibited “sophistication and premeditation.”

“This behavior has become part of a deeply troubling pattern when it comes to this defendant forcing sexual compliance through a personal relationship,” the docs read. “This defendant has proven to be beyond the rehabilitation offered within the Fulton County Juvenile Court process.”

Biermann was arrested in August in connection with an alleged incident that took place in April involving a female classmate, who accused him of sexually assaulting her at a gym in Alpharetta, Georgia. In a subsequent grand jury indictment, he was charged with aggravated child molestation, aggravated sexual battery, aggravated sodomy, false imprisonment and three counts of sexual battery/aggravated sexual battery against a child under 16.

KJ Biermann, 15, Attempts to Avoid Adult Prison Sentence After Indictment

Amid KJ’s sexual assault case, prosecutors uncovered alleged video evidence of the teen having sex with an underage family member under the age of 12. items.title: Blake Shelton Reveals Favorite Part of Being Stepdad to Gwen Stefani's Kids
items.summary:
Blake Shelton can’t help but gush over being a stepdad to wife Gwen Stefani ’s children.

“I guess the most, like, cliché dad thing I do every single day, when the kids get home from school — Apollo, our youngest, we throw the football for about 30 minutes,” Shelton, 50, told Taste of Country in a recent interview. “He’s got this thing, he loves to jump on the trampoline while I throw the football to him so he can do the crazy Odell Beckham catches and DeAndre Hopkins stuff.”

Shelton quipped that throwing the ball to Apollo, 12, “wears [him] out” before sharing how he engages in a more sedentary activity with Zuma, 18.

“Zuma, we’ll spend about 20 minutes with him and his guitar,” he said. “It’s not me showing him stuff. It’s him showing me stuff, you know, ‘Have you heard this song? Have you heard of this artist? Listen to this song.’ It’s almost every single day. I love it. I can’t wait until they get home.”

Blake Shelton's Sweetest Photos With Gwen Stefani's 3 Sons 

Shelton became a stepdad to Stefani’s three sons — Kingston, 20, Zuma and Apollo — when the pair tied the knot in 2021. The No Doubt frontwoman, 57, welcomed her sons with ex-husband Gavin Rossdale , to whom she was married from 2002 to 2016.

Shelton has been candid about his role as a stepparent. In 2021, the country singer explained that he was “very serious” about it, explaining to KFROG hosts, “I don’t know if it’s as hard or harder or not as hard as being an actual, biological parent.”

items.title: Aryna Sabalenka Issues Statement After Alleged Anti-Ukrainian Outburst

“My comment was not directed at Elina,” Sabalenka, 28, posted via Instagram after the match. “I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.”

Svitolina, 32, defeated Sabalenka, who is Belarusian, in the group stage of the 2026 WTA Finals on Friday, November 13. In a clip circulating online , Sabalenka appeared to say “those f***ing Ukrainians, for f***’s sake” in Russian.

items.title: Teen With Cerebral Palsy Died in Tub After Parents Allegedly Left Him at Home
items.summary:
A Connecticut couple has been charged in the death of their 19-year-old son who had cerebral palsy and drowned in a bathtub after they allegedly left him home alone.

Torrington police arrested Martha Almonte and Jeickson Perez-Barahona on charges of criminally negligent homicide and intentional cruelty to persons on Thursday, November 12, court records show.

Their arrests come one year after their son, Marcos Pichardo Almonte , was discovered partly submerged and dead in a bathtub at their Torrington home on November 13, 2025, per Fox affiliate WTIC-TV .

Martha, 39, Marcos’ mother, and Perez-Barahona, 37, his stepfather, drove to Danbury that day without Marcos, who was noticeably thin, and couldn’t walk or stand on his own without help, according to police.

Malnourished 5-Year-Old Dies Weighing Only 19 Pounds, Parents Arrested 

Martha and Perez-Barahona “deliberately limited” Marcos’ ability to access food when they left him, police said, per Patch.com .

They used ratchet straps and cords to lock the refrigerator, freezer and cabinets inside the home and “screwed” a door shut to “deny Marcos’ access” to food kept in the basement, according to authorities.

“The only food available to Marcos were pre-portioned amounts left out for him,” police said, Patch.com reported.

Martha and Perez-Barahona are accused of withholding food from Marcos as punishment for his behavior, according to CT Insider . They allegedly told police that he had once “snuck into the basement” to eat snacks, according to their arrest warrants.

Marcos weighed 68 pounds a week before he died,…
items.t: Teen With Cerebral Palsy Died in Tub After Parents Allegedly Left Him at Home

items.title: Author May Cobb Teases 'All the Little Houses' TV Series, More Sequels
items.summary:
After Netflix found success adapting May Cobb ‘s The Hunting Wives , the author is continuing to expand her book universe with a sequel to All the Little Houses — which is also about to be brought to life on screen.

“When I was writing All the Little Houses, I got almost almost halfway through when I realized I had way too much for one book — and way way too much drama — so I knew that I needed to make it a series,” Cobb exclusively told Us about All the Little Secrets , which is out now.

Cobb was thrilled to return to Longview, Texas, in the sequel but she isn’t sure about another continuation — yet, adding, “I would love to keep that open as a possibility. Right now, we don’t have plans for a book 3 for this. It is a duology, but never say never.”

Set in a small Texas town in the ’80s, All the Little House is centered around several wealthy families whose lives take a turn when a new family moves in. In typical Cobb fashion, chaos, secrets and murder ensues amid a major mystery.

Biggest Differences Between Netflix's ‘The Hunting Wives’ Show and the Book 

All the Little Secrets , meanwhile, picks up after a major cliffhanger. While it is meant to bring the story to a close, news recently broke that Apple TV is developing a TV adaptation of All the Little Houses . 

“Visually, it’ll be really cool to see the farm and the trad wife setup that Abigail creates with her potions and all that. It will be really fun to see the visual representation — or fictionalized version — of my hometown,” Cobb told Us . “Also the characters. I just can’t wait to see how it evolves.”…
items.t: Author May Cobb Teases 'All the Little Houses' TV Series, More Sequels

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Jen Affleck is opening up about her decision to file for divorce from Zac Affleck .

“Somewhere along the way, things changed. We changed,” Jen, 27, wrote via Instagram on Tuesday, November 17. “Neither of us was perfect. We both made mistakes, hurt each other and unfortunately brought out the worst in one another. I wish more than anything that wasn’t how our story unfolded.”

She continued, “Although our marriage wasn’t always healthy, one thing I’ll never take away from Zac is the amazing father he is to our children. Regardless of what happened between us, I’ll always be grateful for that.”

Us previously confirmed that Jen filed a petition for divorce in Utah, where the pair wed, on November 3. The couple — who announced in June that they are expecting baby No. 4 — met on the Mormon dating app Mutual in 2018 before getting engaged. They ultimately got married in 2019.

Mormon Wives' Jen Affleck Said Marriage Was 'Stronger Than Ever' Before Divorce 

“There’s been a lot of conversation surrounding the end of my marriage. And while I know there are people celebrating this new chapter for me, I can’t help but feel a lot of grief,” Jen wrote in her latest social media post. “I think when people talk about divorce, they focus so much on the painful parts of a marriage. But what I’m finding is that grieving the good parts is actually the hardest.”

As her marital struggles play out on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County , which premiered on Thursday, November 12, Jen finds herself “grieving the relationship we once had, the…
items.t: Mormon Wives' Jen Affleck Says She's 'Grieving' Her Marriage Amid Divorce

items.title: Mother's Family Believes She Was Targeted After Being Shot on Her Birthday
items.summary:
A Texas woman was shot to death while she was leaving work on her 35th birthday, and her family believes the killing was targeted as they look for answers.

Stephanie Gonzalez was driving home from work on Sunday, November 15, when she was reportedly shot at around 9:20 p.m. on the C.F. Hawn Freeway in Dallas.

The Dallas Police Department said in a Monday, November 16, statement that Gonzalez, 35, was found inside her vehicle after it had been hit with several bullets. Gonzalez was then taken to a nearby hospital, where she later died from her injuries.

Authorities have not yet publicly identified any suspects in the case, and it’s not clear whether there was a motive for killing Gonzalez or if it was a targeted attack.

Estranged Husband Kidnapped Wife Before Killing Her in Murder-Suicide: Police 

“The motives and circumstances surrounding this offense are still under investigation,” police said in Monday’s statement.

While police are still working to determine exactly what happened, Gonzalez’s family said they believe she was intentionally killed due to the timing of the incident.

“It was her birthday last night. And the way she was attacked was somewhat personal, I believe,” her cousin Vivian Britton told NBC DFW .

Britton also spoke to Fox 4 News about the killing, saying, “She was leaving work. She was maybe 10 minutes away from here, and she was on her way home to see her babies.”

“It’s just tough seeing it’s so senseless. It doesn’t make sense. But we don’t believe in coincidences,” she added. “The way she was attacked was somewhat personal, I believe.”…
items.t: Mother's Family Believes She Was Targeted After Being Shot on Her Birthday

items.summary:
A self-described “sadist” is on trial for the kidnapping and killing of a British woman who flew to Florida to meet him after they met on a fetish website, according to court records.

Dwain Hall , of Ocala, was arrested on murder and kidnapping charges on November 17, 2025, in connection with the discovery of Sonia Exelby’s remains buried in Marion County a month earlier, on October 17, 2025, according to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement .

Authorities in the United Kingdom considered Exelby, 32, endangered and missing after she traveled to Florida and missed her return flight to England on October 13, 2025. U.K. authorities called on the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to help investigate.

During the investigation, evidence on Exelby’s computer indicated “she was suicidal and traveling to the United States to be possibly sexually abused, tortured, and murdered,” according to Hall’s arrest affidavit filed in court and obtained by Us .

Man Waited for Girlfriend to Come Home and Shot Her, Ran Her Over 

Hall, 54, has pleaded not guilty in the case. His trial began in Marion County on Tuesday, November 17, court records show.

Florida investigators learned Exelby had flown from London to Gainesville on October 10, 2025, when Hall picked her up from the airport before they traveled to an Airbnb in Reddick, Florida. He’s accused of fatally stabbing her and getting rid of her body.

Teresa, 54, recalled in her new memoir, The Queen of New Jersey , that unlike meeting the “gracious” Taylor Swift at Coachella Music Festival, “Not every celebrity interaction goes quiet as well.”

She recounted an alleged incident in the book involving an unnamed TV actress that transpired shortly after she rose to fame in 2009 on The Real Housewives of New Jersey .

“[I] was once instructed by my PR team to pose with a well-known TV actress for a photo,” Teresa wrote, noting that the women were both in Los Angeles for an appearance with TV host Mario Lopez . “After we took the photo, I overheard her telling her PR people, ‘Why are you making me take a picture with that woman?’”

Teresa Giudice Asked Taylor Swift 'Do You Know Who I Am?' at Coachella 

The Bravolebrity remembered, “The tone of her voice was so surprising,” writing, “Look, I get if she didn’t know who I was, but to me, that’s just so rude.”

Teresa didn’t identify the actress, but revealed that years later she was back in L.A. having dinner with her husband, Luis “Louie” Ruelas , when a fan came in and asked her for a picture.

“It’s part of this life, and one I happen to enjoy. We took a photo together and chatted for a minute, and then she left us to be seated at her own table,” she shared. “Ten minutes later, who walks in? The actress who had definitely not wanted to take a picture with me all that time ago backstage at Mario Lopez’s show.”

items.title: Court to Hear Christa Pike's Challenge to her 'Indefinite Isolation' in Prison
items.summary:
After Christa Pike’ s attorneys challenged her current prison conditions following her failed execution, a federal court is set to hear arguments in the case.

In an emergency motion filed October 30, Pike’s attorneys called on the court to enforce the terms of a 2024 settlement agreement that ended her 28 years in solitary confinement as the only woman on Tennessee’s death row, allowing for her to have group meals, engage in work and other social and recreational activities.

Pike’s attorneys argued in the filing that the Tennessee Department of Correction is wrongly “holding Ms. Pike in indefinite isolation in the prison infirmary,” away from other women in custody, in violation of that agreement.

In a response filed November 4 viewed by Us , Tennessee Attorney General Jonathan Skrmetti argued the court should deny Pike’s emergency motion, writing prison officials have a “constitutional duty to offer medical care to Pike” and “she can be discharged from the infirmary when medically appropriate.”

Christa Pike Speaks After Botched Execution: 'I Don't Know Why I Survived' 

A judge will hear the opposing arguments from Pike’s legal team and the state on December 1, according to a Friday, November 13, court order.

Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death at the age of 20 after she was convicted of killing her classmate Colleen Slemmer in January 1995, survived two injections of pentobarbital during a botched execution and was taken to a hospital on September 30.

Following her hospital discharge on October 9, her attorneys contend she’s remained wrongly separated from other…

items.title: Is it finally OK to be frank about 2000s pop culture? ‘It was profoundly, cheerfully horrible to women’

In a 2008 episode of BBC Two’s comedy panel show Never Mind the Buzzcocks, the choreographer Arlene Phillips – the only woman on the programme – was told by the host Simon Amstell: “You look like you run a good whore house.” In reply, Phillips told a story with what appeared to be faux sincerity: while working with big stars, she explained, she would sometimes be asked to find dancers with “very special abilities” who might want to party after filming. Another panellist, the TV presenter Dermot O’Leary, mimed picking up a phone and said: “When you’re dancing tonight, do you mind having sex afterwards?” Everyone laughed.

Russell Brand’s imprisonment for rape and sexual assault this week, and allegations of sexual misconduct against the comedian and children’s author David Walliams have prompted scrutiny not only of the men involved, but of those who appeared to enable them. The chatshow host Jonathan Ross has apologised for a 2004 joke, in which he described the 15-year-old British comedy awards as being “like most 15-year-olds: drunk, unpredictable and probably going home with David Walliams”. The latter has denied the allegations made against him in reporting by the Guardian and ITV…

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
items.summary:
One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.

Continue reading...
items.t: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
